name: Frozen II — Movie Companion

options.reply: Watch her face — she loves her people. This isn't boredom.

options.text: Something in her already knows it's calling her home
options.reply: YES. Part of her has always sensed she's not just FROM Arendelle — the voice feels like a memory, not a stranger.
She has every choice. She chooses to go.

quiz.question: Why does Elsa follow the voice even though everyone tells her not to?

sections.Wonder Together: Elsa hears a voice nobody else can hear. Should she follow it, even though it might be dangerous?
sections.For the Grown-up: The sequel opens with a literal call to adventure — a voice only Elsa can hear, pulling her away from a peaceful, settled life. Worth naming: answering a call doesn't mean the old life was wrong. Sometimes peace is exactly what lets you finally hear the next question.

sections.Wonder Together: Kristoff wants to propose to Anna but keeps messing up the moment. Why do you think he's so nervous?
sections.For the Grown-up: A comic scene with a real hurt underneath: Kristoff feels like he doesn't matter as much once Anna's attention turns to her sister and the kingdom. Worth a gentle question for kids: has a friend ever seemed far away even when they were standing right next to you?

options.text: Arendelle asked for too much magic
options.reply: It wasn't about magic — it was about trust, and who broke it first.

options.text: Their king broke a peace agreement and betrayed the Northuldra
options.reply: YES. The dam wasn't really a gift — it was built to weaken the forest people. That betrayal is the root of everything happening now.
Elsa wasn't even born yet — this happened a whole generation earlier.

quiz.question: Why did the forest spirits get angry at Arendelle long ago?

sections.Wonder Together: Elsa and Anna learn their grandfather built the dam as a trick, and it hurt the Northuldra people. How does it feel to find out someone in your own family did something wrong?
sections.For the Grown-up: The film's real rupture, one generation removed: Grandfather Runeard betrayed the Northuldra under a fake peace offer. Same shape as Encanto's river and Moana's dad — an old harm becomes the root of everything that follows. The hard, honest move here for a family conversation: loving your family and admitting it did something wrong are not opposites.

options.reply: The opposite — watch what the spirits do when they finally see her clearly.

options.text: The bridge between people and nature the prophecy was about
options.reply: YES! She was never too much — she was exactly the missing piece, all along.

options.text: A regular queen with a nice singing voice
options.reply: There is SO much more going on — keep watching!

quiz.question: What does Elsa discover she actually is?

sections.Wonder Together: Elsa finds out who she really is and where her powers come from. Does knowing WHERE you're from change WHO you are?
sections.For the Grown-up: The identity question the whole film has been building to — Elsa isn't an anomaly, she's the bridge the two peoples always needed. A gentle note: the movie's answer is that belonging isn't chosen once, it can expand. You can be fully of one place AND discover you're also of another.

options.text: Waits for someone to save her
options.reply: Nobody's coming in this scene — she has to move herself.

options.text: Just the next small right thing, one step at a time
options.reply: YES. Not the whole plan — just one true step. That's often enough to start.
She's tempted to — but watch what she chooses instead.

quiz.question: When Anna feels like giving up, what does she do?

sections.Wonder Together: Anna feels like everything is lost and she doesn't know what to do. What's the smallest thing she decides to do next?
sections.For the Grown-up: Possibly the most quietly important song in either film: when everything feels too big, Anna doesn't solve it all at once — she gets up, and does the next right thing. A genuinely useful tool to name for kids (and ourselves): when overwhelmed, you don't need the whole plan, just the next step.

options.reply: It IS brave — but it's also exactly what repairs the old wrong.

options.text: It undoes the original broken promise to the forest
options.reply: YES. Real repair sometimes means giving something up, not just saying sorry. The water finds its true path again.
This choice is Anna's, and it's not about power — it's about making things right.

quiz.question: Why does breaking the dam actually help, even though it seems risky?

sections.Wonder Together: Anna decides to break the dam — even though it might flood her own kingdom. Why is that the right choice?
sections.For the Grown-up: Restoration that costs something real: repairing the old harm means giving up the thing built on top of it, even though it's now home. This is repair with teeth, not just words — the family (and kingdom) has to actually undo the broken thing, not merely apologize for it. Arendelle survives; it's rebuilt on honesty instead of a lie.

sections.Wonder Together: Elsa becomes the forest's guardian and Anna becomes queen of Arendelle — different homes, still one family. What do you think keeps them close?
sections.For the Grown-up: The ending refuses the idea that growing into who you are means leaving people behind. Elsa expands outward; Anna steps into new responsibility; both stay reachable to each other. A nice closing question: is there a role in OUR family that might be ready to change?

description: Pause-and-talk cards for family movie night with Frozen II (2019). Each item is one pause point: a Wonder Together question for the kid, a For the Grown-up note, and an optional tap-quiz (metadata.quiz). metadata.time is where it fires (approximate — use the extension's nudge buttons); metadata.lens is "discussion" or "repair" (rupture → armor → truth → return → restoration). Our own commentary and questions only — no film dialogue, lyrics, or studio artwork. Part of the Family Watch Club (watch.recursive.eco).
